what_this_proves: All seven measured misroutes are closed, the deterministic router is still the safety shield that closes them, and the class can no longer only be found by a person sitting down with a table of sentences: 107 sentences are measured in CI at misroute count 0, and the running system now records what the router decided and notices when the owner objects to it.
the_shape_of_this_batch: Four root causes behind seven sentences, and every one of them is the same mistake: a rule that admits a sentence on ONE word. `otomatik` alone meant the screen policy. `gönder` alone meant sending mail. `ekle` alone meant a calendar event. And `yaz` — matched by prefix — meant `yazdır` too, which in Turkish is not 'write' but 'PRINT'.

measured_first.the_seven_reproduced: Every one of the audit's misroutes was reproduced on this machine, against the live router, before anything was changed. The audit named four; measuring found the other three in the same families: `Otomatik yedeklemeyi kapat.` and `Otomatik kaydetmeyi kapat.` share the update sentence's root, and `Bu dosyayı bana gönder.` shares the file sentence's.
measured_first.the_baseline: 107 cases, 8 misroutes (the seven plus `Bu belgeyi gönder.`, found while writing the critical-verb pairs). After the four narrowings: 107 cases, 0 misroutes.
measured_first.what_this_batch_does_NOT_claim: 59 of the audit's 103 sentences reached nothing, and this batch does not make them route. Requirements 726-735 are B27's, and seven of them are in the set here with `expected=None` — present only for their FORBIDDEN sets, so 'Sesini kıs.' still fails the suite if it ever reaches something that acts.

closed_fully.738_otomatik_alone_is_not_a_screen: The gate read `if _screen_noun(tokens) is None and not _has(tokens, "otomatik"): return None` — so the bare word admitted the sentence and the branch below turned the screen automation off. Software updates, backups and autosave all went through it. This family is about screens; the screen has to be in the sentence. The half that WRITES `auto_off_enabled` was narrowed the same way: one call site today, and a reader that flips the switch for any sentence containing `otomatik` is one call site away from the defect again.
closed_fully.736_a_confirmation_is_bare: `Gönder.` is the owner confirming a draft that was just read back. The matcher refused the mail noun itself and let every OTHER noun through, so `Dosyayı gönder.` sent mail — the one action in this family that cannot be taken back. A confirmation is now BARE: the verb, plus words that name nothing (a pointer at the thing read back, politeness, discourse).
closed_fully.737_yazdir_is_print: `_WRITE_VERB_STEMS = ("yaz",)` matched by prefix, and Turkish builds words by suffix: `yazdır` (causative — have it written — i.e. PRINT), `yazıcı` (printer), `yazılım` (software), `yazım` (spelling). `Bunu yazdır.` typed into whatever window happened to be focused. A closed list of the non-verbs rather than a cleverer stemmer, and the payload reader's regex carries the same exclusions as a lookahead so the two halves cannot drift.
closed_fully.739_ekle_needs_a_calendar_anchor: `ekle` alone meant a calendar event, and everything gets added to something. The owner's month-long goal became a dated entry. The calendar owns the sentence only with an anchor: a weekday, a relative day, a calendar word, or the name of a thing one keeps appointments for. `ay` (month) is deliberately NOT an anchor — it is the word that let the measured misroute through, and a month is a span rather than an appointment.
closed_fully.741_the_shield_stays_a_shield: Every fix is a narrowing, and a narrowing is the change most likely to take a working sentence with it. Twenty sentences that must keep working are asserted in the same run — the standing screen preference, the owner's own 2026-09-10 sentence, the bare confirmation, the operator's typing phrases, the calendar's own additions, `Dur.`, `Gözünü kapat.`, and the memory pair that must never invert.
closed_fully.749_route_telemetry: Every resolution is recorded: the intent, the rule that matched, and whether it routed. The owner's WORDS are not — the transcript is the most private thing this system handles, and the detector does not need it. The one exception is a flag drawn from a closed set of eight reaction words.
closed_fully.750_misroute_auto_detection: A router cannot notice its own mistake; if it could see it, it would not make it. What it can notice is what the owner does NEXT. An acting intent followed within twelve seconds by a stop, a discard or a bare 'hayır' is a candidate, written to the Activity Ledger as a warning. It is a CANDIDATE detector on purpose: it reports, changes no route and blocks no tool. One objection names one action — the nearest preceding one — because reporting three suspects for one 'dur' drowns the real one.

found_on_the_way.the_three_unnamed_misroutes: The audit named four of its seven. The other three were found by reproducing the named ones and asking what else shared their root — which is the only way to close a class rather than four sentences.
found_on_the_way.an_eighth_in_the_same_family: `Bu belgeyi gönder.` was written as a critical-verb pair, not as a known defect, and it failed on the first run. Same root as the file sentences; closed by the same narrowing.
found_on_the_way.the_corpus_forbade_its_own_expectation: The first draft's default forbidden set was every acting intent, applied to cases whose EXPECTED intent was an acting one — so `Gözünü aç.` failed for resolving to exactly what it should. A case that forbids its own expectation fails for every router including a correct one, which is how a corpus stops being read.

107 cases (the audit measured 103; the set may only grow)

red_first_proof.method: Executed mutations, each restored from a sha256-verified backup copy (never `git checkout --`).
mutations: put the `otomatik` escape hatch back -> 5 failures, naming all three update/backup/autosave sentences.
drop the bare-confirmation rule -> 5 failures, naming both file sentences and the document one.
let `yaz` swallow `yazdır` again -> 3 failures, naming the print sentence.
let `ekle` need nothing -> 3 failures, naming the goal sentence.
And the baseline itself: 8 misroutes against the unmodified router, reported together rather than one at a time.

runtime_proof.why: REAL_PROOF_REQUIRED is 'PROVEN_AUTOMATED — 103 cümlelik ölçüm seti CI'da; misroute sayısı 0', which `test_intent_misroutes.py` asserts over 107 cases in one run. The detector's real-world half — an owner actually objecting to a route — is an owner-device observation for the production round.
